newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Greenall raises Capex programm.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Greenall raises Capex programm.

text.p: British pub-to-hotel company Greenalls Group will spend more on expanding its pub restaurant and managed pubs, Village Leisure and De Vere's golf hotels next year, chief executive Lord Daresbury said on Monday.
"We plan to increase our capital expenditure programme from 175 million pounds in the current financial year to over 200 million next year," said Daresbury in an interview.
"This expenditure is currently 70 percent offensive and 30 percent defensive, in other words spent on maintenance, but next year we will spend 150 million offensively as against 125," he added.

Earlier, the company posted a 12 percent increase in its half year profit before tax excluding exceptional items of 63.9 million stg. Exceptional items amounted to 6.2 million, including pub reorganisation costs of 7.3 million which the group announced in March.
Brokers forecasts for pretax profits ranged from 61.1 million to 66.0 milllion.
Daresbury said the company has made further progress since its half year results, "its very much the same as before, satisfactory and we are hoping that will continue."
The company was held back in the first half by continued difficult trading in some of its drinks-led managed houses, especially in the north west of England.
"(Perhaps) it's the strength of the pound putting pressure on the manufactoring sector, which means there maybe less disposable income available," said Daresbury.
"Moving 245 pubs to tenanted was aimed at sorting this out. These are pubs in secondary locations. I think that move is a radical move and it has addressed the problem," he added.

The group's pubs and restaurants division reported a 12.7 percent increase in trading profit to 45.1 million stg. Profits from its de Vere hotels rose 19.4 percent to 12.7 million, with the hotels and leisure division as whole posting a 28 percent increase in profits to 16.66 million.
De Vere hotels achieved room rates 15.9 percent higher at 62 pounds and the company plans to develop its golf hotels where returns are higher.
"Our hotel figures compare very well with Stakis and Vaux, and Marriott RevPar Whitbread announced was up only 16 percent," said Daresbury.
Greenalls' franchised pubs and wholesaling business reported a 12.7 percent improvement in trading profit to 24.3 million.
The company's shares were off 1p at 493 in early trade, against the background of a softer start to trading on London's stockmarket.
